drug_class: GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist (dual incretin receptor agonist)
purpose: Tirzepatide is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes (Mounjaro). It is also approved to help with weight loss in adults who are overweight or obese (Zepbound). It works best when combined with healthy eating and exercise.
how_it_works: Tirzepatide mimics two natural hormones in your body called GIP and GLP-1, which are released after you eat. These hormones tell your pancreas to release insulin when your blood sugar rises, help lower the amount of sugar your liver puts out, and signal your brain that you feel full so you eat less. Because it targets two pathways instead of one, it tends to be very effective at lowering blood sugar and reducing appetite.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, and stomach pain or upset. These usually happen most when you first start the medication or when your dose is increased, and they often get better over time. Eating smaller meals and avoiding greasy or spicy foods can help.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you or anyone in your family has ever had a type of thyroid cancer called medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or a condition called MEN2, because this medication may not be safe for you. It can rarely cause serious problems like pancreatitis (severe stomach pain), gallbladder disease, or low blood sugar especially if you take other diabetes medicines. Do not use this medication if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Always let your healthcare team know all the medications you take.
typical_dosing: Tirzepatide is given as a once-weekly injection under the skin, usually in the stomach, thigh, or upper arm. The starting dose is typically 2.5 mg once a week for the first four weeks to help your body adjust. Your doctor will gradually increase the dose every four weeks, up to a maximum of 15 mg once a week, based on how well it is working and how you are tolerating it.
